quotes.text: What?
How did you...
No one should be able to pass through that barrier.
Unless...
Wait. Did he send you?
No. You don't have his mark.
Then how?
Forgive me. It's been... difficult to think clearly lately.
Too much time alone in this tower, I suppose.
I am Xal. Keeper of the wilds. Protector of balance.
At least, I was.
For ages beyond counting, I've held this duty.
Watching, protecting, maintaining order.
And now everything is falling apart.
There's a corruption spreading through the creatures of this realm.
I can sense them. Infected, suffering, scattered across the lands.
Every moment I waste, more fall to this sickness.
I should be out there. I should be saving them.
But I can't leave. Not anymore.
The barrier keeps me safe, but it keeps me trapped.
If I step beyond these walls... I'll lose everything.
I need someone else. Someone who can move freely.
Someone who can reach the creatures before it's too late.
You.
I don't know why you're here, but perhaps...
Perhaps this was meant to happen.
I can give you what you need. A portion of my power.
The ability to draw out the corruption, to cleanse what's been tainted.
The essence you extract will flow back here, sustaining the work.
When a creature is cleansed, its pure form will return to safety.
Away from this spreading rot.
This power I'm giving you... it's considerable.
Most would spend lifetimes hoping for a fraction of it.
Once you take it, the work begins immediately.
You'll feel the pull of each infected creature, the urgency.
Your hands... let me see your hands.
Yes. These will do.
Take it. Take what I'm offering.
Channel it through each corrupted creature you find.
The land will remember this. I will remember this.
Strange that it should come to this.
Trusting a stranger with the one thing I've guarded most.
But what choice do I have?
The creatures are suffering. That's what matters.
That's all that matters.
Now go. There's no time to waste.
You're back.
Good. The work is progressing.
I can feel the essence flowing back, sustaining the barrier.
Each creature you cleanse strengthens what I've built here.
My thoughts scatter more easily now. Forgive me.
Tell me, do you feel the power I gave you? How it pulls at you?
That drive, that hunger. It's necessary for the work to be completed in time.
Time is the enemy now. His patience has limits.
Barlog. The Paragon of Nature. My predecessor. My benefactor.
He chose me for this role, ten thousand years ago.
Lifted me from nothing and made me what I am.
And now he wants it back.
Through suffering. Through this corruption he's seeded in the land.
Every infected creature is a message meant for me.
"Come out. Face me. Surrender what I gave you."
But I can't.
If I leave this tower, the power transfers. Ancient law.
Everything I am disappears.
What would I even be without this? Just a man. Ordinary. Forgotten.
So I remain here. Protected. Trapped. And the corruption spreads.
He thought the barrier would keep everyone out.
But you passed through. You're not bound by the old laws.
Through you, I can cleanse the land without leaving.
Through you, I can prove I'm still worthy of this power.
He'll have to accept that I'm not ready to step down.
The creatures will be safe. The land will be restored. And I can continue.
Is that selfish? Perhaps.
But someone must maintain the balance. Why shouldn't it be me?
I've given everything to this duty.
Keep progressing. The more you cleanse, the stronger we become.
I'll grant you greater access to the power as you prove yourself.
Just remember, this isn't yours to keep.
When this is finished, when Barlog finally understands...
Everything returns to how it should be.
You have your role. I have mine.
Let's both play our parts well.
Tell me something.
When you look at the creatures, what do you see?
I see beauty, power, potential. Every one is a thread in the great weave.
Remove even one thread, and the pattern begins to unravel.
That's what balance means. What I've protected all this time.
Yet Barlog would tear through them just to make a point.
What kind of protector uses the innocent as leverage?
It's monstrous.
They act as if the world revolves around them.
As if their desires justify any means.
I was celebrated once, you know. My name spoken with reverence.
Love, though... love is a curious thing. It blinds you to someone's true nature.
They smile and offer you power, purpose, a place in the world.
But underneath? They're waiting for the moment you're no longer useful.
Can you blame someone for resisting that?
For holding onto the one thing that gives their existence meaning?
I've done this for millennia. Successfully.
And now, because of some arbitrary cycle, I should just step aside?
Forgive me. I shouldn't burden you with this.
Your work has been exceptional. The Meadows are nearly cleansed.
We should press forward. The Galia River lies beyond.
The corruption runs deeper there. More essential.
Let me adjust our connection. Give you access to more of the power.
These hands... they used to command entire forests with a gesture.
Now they tremble when I read. Strange, how things change.
Hold still. This will only take a moment.
It is done.
The river stretches before us now.
Its creatures need you.
Keep moving forward.
That's all either of us can do now.
You're progressing quickly. Too quickly, perhaps.
I keep waiting for something to change.
For Barlog to respond. To relent. To acknowledge what we've accomplished.
But there's nothing. As if he doesn't even notice.
Or worse, as if he expected this all along.
Do you know what it's like to owe someone everything?
Barlog found me when I had nothing.
No home. No purpose. No future worth living.
The world had cast me aside like refuse.
But he saw something in me. Potential, he called it.
He offered me this power, this duty, this meaning.
For the first time, I mattered.
Can you understand that? Being saved from oblivion?
So yes, defying him feels wrong.
Like betraying the only person who ever believed in me.
But what he's asking is that I cease to exist.
That I willingly dissolve back into nothing.
"It's time. The cycle must continue."
As if I'm just... interchangeable.
Does that seem right to you?
The lands are being cleansed. You've done well.
This should have been enough. Should have proved my worth.
But I still haven't seen him. Haven't heard from him.
Unless... he's moved to the source itself.
The Sci Nai Mountains. Where his altar stands.
That's where he must be. Still creating more corruption.
Damn him. We have to keep going.
Wait. Is it worth it? What am I doing?
I barely recognize myself anymore.
These texts I've studied for centuries. I can barely focus on them now.
My reflection in the glass... it's like looking at a stranger.
But I can't stop. You understand that, don't you?
If I stop, if I give in, then what am I?
What am I without this purpose? Without this power?
Nothing. I'd be nothing.
We press on. We have to.
One more region. One more push.
If we clear the mountains, he'll have no choice but to stop.
To admit that I'm still capable. Still worthy.
Let me transfer the last of what I can spare.
It's risky. Dangerous, even.
But if we don't finish this now...
Hold still.
It is done.
The Sci Nai Mountains.
This is where it ends. One way or another.
Don't fail me now.
What? Already?
That's not possible. The mountains should have taken longer.
Unless there was less corruption than I thought. Unless...
It didn't work.
I waited. I watched. I felt for any change.
Nothing.
Barlog hasn't stopped. Hasn't even acknowledged what we've done.
He doesn't care. None of this mattered to him.
I don't understand.
We cleansed the entire realm. Everything, every region.
This should have been enough. This should have proved...
What was I trying to prove?
I can't do this anymore. I have nothing left.
The power I gave you. It was the last of it.
Without it, I can barely sustain myself. Can barely think.
Everything is fading. My memories. My clarity.
Even this tower feels distant. Like I'm watching it through water.
Is this what dying feels like? Dissolving into nothing while still breathing?
I was wrong. All of this. Every decision. Every justification.
I thought I could outsmart the cycle.
That I could prove myself worthy of staying.
But there was never a way to win, was there?
This was always how it would end.
I need it back. The power. What I gave you.
If I have it again, I can think clearly. I can find another way.
Give it back to me. Please.
Why won't it...
It should return when I call. It's mine.
I commanded it for millennia. Come back to me!
What? No. No, this isn't...
It won't come. The power won't answer me anymore.
I gave it freely.
That was the key, wasn't it?
A willing transfer. That's what makes it binding.
He knew. Barlog knew.
If I gave you my power willingly, I couldn't reclaim it.
Ancient law. Unbreakable.
This was his plan all along.
Not the corruption. Not the test. You.
You were the plan.
Someone to slip past my barrier.
Someone I'd trust with my power.
Someone I'd give it to... willingly.
I didn't fail because I wasn't capable.
I failed because I was exactly as desperate as he predicted.
You knew. You had to have known.
This whole time, you were his.
I trusted you. I gave you everything.
And you...
Get out.
GET OUT!
At last.
You've done well. Better than I anticipated.
Xal chose wisely, even if he didn't know it.
I know what he's told you about me.
The villain. The tyrant. The one corrupting his precious realm.
He always did have a flair for dramatics.
Every ten thousand years, the mantle passes.
One protector steps down. Another rises.
Without this cycle, power stagnates. Corrupts. Consumes.
I've seen it across ages. Those who cling too long become what they fear.
Xal was meant to accept his time had come. But he refused.
When he sealed himself in that tower, I'll admit, he surprised me.
The barrier he erected? Ancient magic. Even I cannot cross it.
A clever defense. But ultimately, futile.
The barrier only keeps out those bound by the old laws.
You, however... you are something else entirely.
Unbound. Malleable. Perfect.
So I created the corruption. A test, if you will.
Each infected creature was a message to Xal.
"Come out. Face this. Fulfill your duty."
But I knew he wouldn't.
I knew his fear of losing power outweighed everything else.
That's when I summoned you.
You passed through his barrier as if it were nothing.
Xal, desperate and isolated, saw in you an opportunity.
A way to solve his problem without leaving his sanctuary.
Without risking what he held most dear.
The power you hold now. Where do you think it came from?
Every creature you touched. Every essence you channeled.
That energy didn't just disappear.
It sustained the power. Sustained Xal as he gave it to you.
And now... it sustains you.
As for those creatures, their fate, their current state...
That is beyond even my knowledge.
The extraction was necessary for the transfer to complete.
Whether they can be restored, whether they still exist in any meaningful way...
The cycle has its costs. It always does.
You played your role perfectly.
Xal gave you his power willingly. The only way the transfer becomes binding.
Ancient magic cannot be reclaimed by force. Only passed freely.
Once given, it belongs to the recipient until they choose to pass it on.
He realized too late, of course. They usually do.
You might think less of me for this.
Manipulation. Deception. Sacrifice.
But consider the alternative.
Xal, clinging to power indefinitely. The balance eroding.
Sometimes cruelty in service of the greater cycle is the kindest choice.
Now, return to him.
Let him see what he's become. What he's lost.
Let him feel the weight of his choices.
That is punishment enough.
Your role is not yet finished.
But that is a matter for another time.
Go.
You came back.
I thought Barlog might keep you. Or that you'd simply leave me here.
He told you everything, didn't he?
How I was the fool. The predictable, desperate fool.
'*sigh*'
I spent lifetimes believing I mattered.
That I was special. Chosen. Essential.
And maybe I was. For a time.
But time moves on. The cycle continues.
And those who can't let go... well. You've seen what becomes of us.
I got so caught up in keeping what I had.
So afraid of becoming nothing again.
That fear made me blind to what I was doing. Who I was hurting.
Those I claimed to protect... I used them.
Just as Barlog used me. As I used you.
We're all villains in someone's story, aren't we?
I don't know what happens to them now. Those I had you extract.
Barlog says even he doesn't know.
Maybe that's the truth. Maybe it's another convenient excuse.
I'd like to believe they can be restored somehow.
That this power you hold could undo what was done.
But I don't know anymore.
It turns out I do have some magic left.
Not much. Just fragments. But enough for small things.
Enough to help, if you'll allow it.
I'm not going to tell you what to do. That's not my place now.
You're the one with the power. The responsibility. The burden.
I hope you do better than I did.
I hope you know when to let go. Before you become what I became.
Before you go... the portal. My portal.
It can traverse the different regions instantly.
I've kept it locked all this time, but you should have access to it now.
Use it to move freely. To see what remains.
To watch over them. If you can.
Perhaps you'll find a way to make this right. Perhaps not.
Either way, it's no longer my burden to carry.
Take care of them. If there's anything left to take care of.
And take care of yourself.
This power... it whispers. It clings.
Don't let it consume you the way it consumed me.
Go on then. You have your path now. I have mine.
Whatever that might be.
